preamble: The voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ] was fortited to the voiced velar stop [g] in the Northeastern dialects of Pashto, in parallel with the shift of [ʂ] to [x]. The conservative Southwestern (Kandahar) dialect keeps the retroflex.

examples.note: The letter ږ is [ʐ] in Kandahar Pashto and [g] in the Northeastern dialects. In the Northwestern dialect it is [ʝ]. The shift is placed in the medieval period and appears to have been still incomplete when the orthography was fixed in the 16th century.

sources: MacKenzie, D. N. (1987). Pashto. In B. Comrie (ed.), The World's Major Languages. Croom Helm.
